name: Fast and Slow Pointers
description: Also known as Floyd's cycle detection, this pattern uses two pointers moving at different speeds. The fast pointer moves two steps, the slow pointer moves one. If there is a cycle, they will eventually meet inside the cycle.
how_to_identify: Problems about cycles, the middle of a linked list, or detecting loops without extra space.
use_cases: Detecting a cycle in a linked list
Finding the middle node of a linked list
Finding the start of a cycle
template: Initialize slow = head, fast = head. Advance fast by two and slow by one. If fast reaches None there is no cycle; if they meet, a cycle exists. To find the cycle start, reset one pointer to head and advance both one step.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to guard against fast.next being None before advancing two steps.
Using a hash set of visited nodes instead of constant space.
